sources.name: Soil Bulk Density in Europe
sources.publisher: European Commission Joint Research Centre, European Soil Data Centre
source_locators: Dataset description: 6,140 samples at 0-10 cm and 5,684 samples at 10-20 cm from LUCAS 2018, spatialized to 100 m across the EU and UK.
Key findings: croplands have almost 1.5 times higher bulk density than woodlands; model R-squared is 0.66.

metric_contract.unit: measured bulk density and modeled packing-density class, affected arable-land share, measured yield reduction and persistence
metric_contract.geography: European Union and United Kingdom LUCAS soil-sampling domain
metric_contract.boundary: The assessment is anchored to measured bulk-density cores and a documented packing-density model. It does not infer compaction from machinery, crop type or agricultural intensity alone, and it is not extrapolated beyond the EU and UK.

uncertainty: Packing density is a modeled proxy derived from bulk density and clay content, and the published model reports R-squared of 0.66. The 3.2 percent compacted share applies to arable land in the European assessment domain, not all agricultural land globally. The greater-than-35-percent yield reduction and 17-year persistence are measured evidence summarized by ESDAC, but they are not asserted to occur at every compacted LUCAS pixel. EU-27 plus the United Kingdom is used only as the represented assessment coverage.
